title: [B1 • Band 5.0] Bài 104: The Terracotta Army: Ancient Guardians in Clay
passageHtml:
READING PASSAGE — B1 (BAND 5.0) • TEST 104

The Terracotta Army: Ancient Guardians in Clay

Paragraph 1. In March 1974, during a severe drought in Shaanxi province, China, a group of local farmers started digging a deep well east of the ancient capital of Xi'an. A few metres down, their shovels hit hard, baked clay. Digging further, they pulled up pottery pieces, bronze arrowheads, and a life-sized clay human head. Realizing the finds might be important, local officials invited archaeological teams to examine the site. This ordinary farm project soon revealed one of the greatest discoveries of the twentieth century: the Terracotta Army of Emperor Qin Shi Huang.

Paragraph 2. Qin Shi Huang conquered six rival kingdoms to unite China in 221 BCE. Believing he would continue ruling in the afterlife, he ordered the construction of a massive underground tomb complex soon after becoming emperor as a teenager. Later historical records written by the Han historian Sima Qian state that over 700,000 forced workers and skilled artisans laboured for nearly forty years to finish the site, filling it with palaces and thousands of clay soldiers, archers, chariots, and horses.

Paragraph 3. Excavations proved that building this army relied on clever mass-production methods. State workshops pressed basic body parts—such as feet, legs, arms, and torsos—from coarse local clay using reusable hollow moulds. However, artists then carved unique hairstyles, ears, and facial expressions onto each warrior by hand so that no two figures looked alike. To ensure strict quality control, master craftsmen stamped their personal names onto hidden areas of the statues before firing.

Paragraph 4. Originally, the terracotta soldiers were not the plain grey or brown statues seen in museums today. Every warrior was painted in bright mineral colours, including red, green, blue, and a synthetic purple. These colours were brushed over a protective base layer of natural lacquer taken from Chinese trees. Sadly, when newly dug statues meet northern China's dry air, this ancient base layer dries out within minutes, shrinks, and peels the bright paint away.

Paragraph 5. To prevent this rapid damage, modern scientists now spray freshly uncovered statues with special protective chemical solutions or seal them inside damp plastic containers. Meanwhile, testing on the real bronze swords and spears held by the warriors showed that their metal blades stayed remarkably sharp and free of rust for over two millennia, thanks to the natural chemistry of the surrounding earth.

groups.title: Questions 6–9
groups.instructions:
Do the following statements agree with the information given in the passage?
Write TRUE, FALSE or NOT GIVEN.

steps: Đoạn 1: "started digging a deep well" → Từ cần điền: well.
Đoạn 3: "using reusable hollow moulds" → Từ cần điền: moulds.
Đoạn 3: "stamped their personal names onto hidden areas..." → Từ cần điền: names.
Đoạn 4: "protective base layer of natural lacquer" → Từ cần điền: lacquer.
Đoạn 5: "natural chemistry of the surrounding earth" → Từ cần điền: earth.

q6.text: The Shaanxi farmers immediately knew that the clay head was over two thousand years old.

steps: Đoạn 1: Chính quyền địa phương thấy có thể quan trọng nên gọi chuyên gia, hoàn toàn không nói nông dân có biết ngay niên đại hơn 2000 năm tuổi hay không → Chọn NOT GIVEN.

q7.text: All clay soldiers in the tomb were given identical facial features.

steps: Đoạn 3: Nghệ nhân chạm khắc bằng tay nên "no two figures looked alike" (không tượng nào giống nhau) → Chọn FALSE.

q8.text: In ancient times, the terracotta statues were left completely unpainted.

steps: Đoạn 4: "Every warrior was painted in bright mineral colours" → Chọn FALSE.

q9.text: Modern scientists use chemical sprays to protect newly uncovered statues from dry air.

steps: Đoạn 5: "spray freshly uncovered statues with special protective chemical solutions..." → Chọn TRUE.
